text:
alex: Heads up — overnight jobs on gpu-node-07 started spitting Xid errors (mostly Xid 13, a couple Xid 79). ECC counters on GPU0 climbed from 0 -> 24. Not going to put this back in rotation until we can reproduce or confirm root cause.

priya: Agreed. We should run a multi-stage repro: drain node, full mem/stress soak, nv-bug-report, and power-cycle retries. I'd set a minimum 12h soak.

sam: +1. Add continuous nvidia-smi monitoring (util + mem), and run stressapptest or cuda_memtest. If Xid reappears, capture dmesg lines and PCIe errors.

maria: Plan (ops steps):
```
# drain & isolate
kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
ssh root@gpu-node-07
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo systemctl stop docker || sudo systemctl stop containerd

# baseline dumps
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,UTILIZATION,PCI > /var/tmp/gpu-q-$(date +%s).txt
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 400 > /var/tmp/dmesg-$(date +%s).txt
sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output-file /var/tmp/nvr-bug-$(date +%s).tar.gz

# start soak (run as nohup or screen)
nohup /opt/tools/stressapptest -W -M -s 43200 -G > /var/log/gpu-soak.log 2>&1 &
# also run a small CUDA memtest if available
nohup /opt/tools/cuda_memtest --duration=12h > /var/log/cuda-memtest.log 2>&1 &
```
Check logs for lines like: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:xx:00:00): 79" or "GPU 0: ECC error".

priya: We'll want DCGM running too to capture power/thermal trends: `dcgmi dmon --csv` and collect every 1s. Also add `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` as fallback.

ken: If you can reproduce Xid within the 12h window, mark the card "candidate for RMA" and schedule replacement. If it's intermittent, extend to 48h with power-cycle between runs (power-off 60s). Historically some flaky cards only fail after a warm-up cycle.

sam: Diagnostic checklist for whoever picks this up:
- collect /var/log/messages and dmesg around the time of Xid
- nvidia-smi -q output
- nvidia-bug-report tarball
- PCIe AER / IOMMU errors
- GPU firmware version and driver (match against known bad builds)
If you can reproduce, attach bug report and output to the ticket.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0453. Pager duty ping sent to infra-oncall.

alex: I'll run the first soak tonight and post logs here. Leaving node drained. tagging @maria for upload path and @ken for RMA workflow.

maria: Upload path: s3://redwood-gpu-faults/gpu-node-07/1745004321/ ; please include bugreport + dmesg + soak logs. Also create a short postmortem note in /confluence/gpu-fleet/ if replaced.

alex: Started soak at 23:12 UTC. stressapptest + cuda_memtest launched, dcgm dump running. I'll check in AM. :thumbsup:

priya: Quick reminder: use `rictl node cordon gpu-node-07` if you want to prevent scheduler from touching it while you debug.

alex: update — 03:43 UTC: saw an Xid 13 on GPU0 after ~4h into soak, replicated twice within 30m. Captured dmesg snippet and bugreport. Uploading now.

maria: Thanks. Given repeatable Xid, let's treat this as a failing card. Ken, can you coordinate a replacement N+1 and RMA flow?

ken: On it. I'll trigger node replace job and order RMA. Procedure: `rictl node replace gpu-node-07 --preserve-labels` then keep a hotspare in the same AZ. Also scheduling hardware swap Monday morning unless urgent.

sam: For records: observed errors were Xid 13 with backtrace pointing to nvkm_channel and context switch. No obvious PCIe link down messages. ECC corrected count incremented.

alex: Will paste minimal dmesg + nvidia-smi excerpts here and link s3. Thanks all.

priya: Nice triage. For future: add a quick `gpu-burnin` job template that ops can spin up on any drained node (12h default, with automatic bugreport collection on Xid). Keeps handoff smoother.

maria: Agreed — I'll draft a runbook and add it to infra runbooks.

ops-bot: NOTE: Node gpu-node-07 marked OutOfService in cluster catalog.

ken: Closing loop once RMA landed and replacement node passes a 48h soak.

alex: final: logs uploaded -> s3://redwood-gpu-faults/gpu-node-07/1745004321/ ; node is offline. Will add postmortem when replacement completes.
